# Full-circle polar chart is inconsistent with its own axis

I have a polar chart whose angular axis spans the whole circle, one categorical series per spoke,
with a tooltip enabled.

Hovering it gives me this, and the result depends on which part of the circle I point at:

![image](/app/.harbor_assets/bug.png)

And this is what it draws for the data I passed in, with no pointer involved at all:

![image](/app/.harbor_assets/mismatch.png)

## What is the expected behavior?

The chart should be self-consistent everywhere on the circle: for any spoke, the series it is
labelled with, the series drawn on it, and the series a hover near it resolves to must all be the
same one — and a hover must resolve to the spoke nearest the pointer, reporting that series' own
point on the chart.

This has to hold for any number of series, and whatever start and end angle the circle is laid out
with.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Behavioral verifier for recharts__recharts-5099-mm.
Reward policy: 1.0 all f2p+p2p pass, 0.5 partial, 0.0 no f2p.
"""
import json, os, re, xml.etree.ElementTree as ET

CONF   = json.load(open("/tests/config.json"))
F2P    = CONF["f2p"]
P2P    = CONF["p2p"]
REPORT = "/logs/verifier/report.xml"
REWARD = "/logs/verifier/reward.txt"

def load_results():
    results = {}
    if not os.path.exists(REPORT):
        return results
    try:
        tree = ET.parse(REPORT)
    except ET.ParseError:
        return results
    for tc in tree.iter("testcase"):
        classname = tc.get("classname", "") or ""
        name      = tc.get("name", "") or ""
        ident     = f"{classname}::{name}".strip("::")
        failed    = any(c.tag in ("failure", "error") for c in tc)
        skipped   = any(c.tag == "skipped" for c in tc)
        results[ident] = "skip" if skipped else ("fail" if failed else "pass")
    return results

def matched(idents, results):
    out = {}
    for ident in idents:
        hit = next((v for k, v in results.items() if ident in k or re.search(re.escape(ident), k)), None)
        out[ident] = hit or "missing"
    return out

def main():
    r      = load_results()
    f2p    = matched(F2P, r)
    p2p    = matched(P2P, r)
    f2p_pass = [k for k, v in f2p.items() if v == "pass"]
    p2p_pass = [k for k, v in p2p.items() if v == "pass"]
    all_f2p  = len(f2p_pass) == len(F2P) and len(F2P) > 0
    all_p2p  = len(p2p_pass) == len(P2P)
    if all_f2p and all_p2p:
        reward = 1.0
    elif f2p_pass and (not all_p2p or not all_f2p):
        reward = 0.5
    else:
        reward = 0.0
    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(REWARD), exist_ok=True)
    open(REWARD, "w").write(str(reward))
    print(json.dumps({"reward": reward, "f2p": f2p, "p2p": p2p}))

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

# Full-circle polar chart is inconsistent with its own axis

I have a polar chart whose angular axis spans the whole circle, one categorical series per spoke,
with a tooltip enabled.

Hovering it gives me this, and the result depends on which part of the circle I point at:

![image](/app/.harbor_assets/bug.png)

And this is what it draws for the data I passed in, with no pointer involved at all:

![image](/app/.harbor_assets/mismatch.png)

## What is the expected behavior?

The chart should be self-consistent everywhere on the circle: for any spoke, the series it is
labelled with, the series drawn on it, and the series a hover near it resolves to must all be the
same one — and a hover must resolve to the spoke nearest the pointer, reporting that series' own
point on the chart.

This has to hold for any number of series, and whatever start and end angle the circle is laid out
with.
===
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Behavioral verifier for recharts__recharts-5099-mm.
# Applies test.patch, runs f2p+p2p vitest tests, computes reward.
# NEVER greps source for the fix: reward comes from the test report only.
set -uo pipefail

mkdir -p /logs/verifier
STDOUT_LOG=/logs/verifier/test-stdout.txt
STDERR_LOG=/logs/verifier/test-stderr.txt
REPORT=/logs/verifier/report.xml

: > "$STDOUT_LOG"
: > "$STDERR_LOG"

ensure_reward() {
  [ -f /logs/verifier/reward.txt ] || echo 0 > /logs/verifier/reward.txt
}
trap ensure_reward EXIT

cd /app || { echo "no /app" | tee -a "$STDERR_LOG"; exit 1; }

# ── Step 1: restore any test paths the agent may have edited ─────────────────
# Paths come from the `diff --git a/... b/...` headers so binary diffs and
# renames are also reset correctly (a `+++ b/` grep would silently skip them).
echo "== restoring test files to harbor_base ==" | tee -a "$STDOUT_LOG"
test_patch_paths=$(
  { sed -n 's#^diff --git a/\(.*\) b/.*#\1#p' /tests/test.patch
    sed -n 's#^diff --git a/.* b/\(.*\)#\1#p' /tests/test.patch; } | sort -u
)
# The test harness itself is reset too, so the scoring run cannot be neutered by
# editing the runner config, the global setup or the shared test helpers.
harness_paths="vitest.config.mts test/vitest.setup.ts test/helper/mockGetBoundingClientRect.ts
test/helper/mockHTMLElementProperty.ts test/helper/assertNotNull.ts test/helper/consoleWarningToError.ts
test/helper/createSelectorTestCase.tsx package.json"
for _p in $test_patch_paths $harness_paths; do
  git -C /app checkout harbor_base -- "$_p" 2>/dev/null || rm -f "/app/$_p" 2>/dev/null || true
done

# ── Step 2: apply test.patch ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
echo "== applying test.patch ==" | tee -a "$STDOUT_LOG"
git apply --binary /tests/test.patch 2>>"$STDERR_LOG" \
  || git apply /tests/test.patch 2>>"$STDERR_LOG" \
  || patch -p1 -i /tests/test.patch 2>>"$STDERR_LOG" \
  || { echo "ERROR: could not apply test.patch" | tee -a "$STDERR_LOG"; exit 1; }

# ── Step 3: install pinned test-only deps ────────────────────────────────────
